newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress inducts reformer into top panel.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress inducts reformer into top panel.

text.p: India's Congress Party inducted the chief architect of economic reforms, former finance minister Dr Manmohan Singh, into the party's top decision-making panel on Sunday, its president said.
"My first job is to nominate Manmohan Singh as member of Congress Working Committee (CWC)," Sitaram Kesri the president of country's oldest political party told a news conference.
The CWC will now have 20 members.
Singh, a former university professor, was finance miniser in the government of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao which lost power in general elections this year.
Known for his integrity and clean image, Singh's induction into the party's top brass takes place when the Congress is dogged by various corruption charges.
Rao finds the legal noose tightening around himself with the federal police filing charges against him in two cases involving forgery and cheating.

When asked whether Singh would be invited to lead the Congress in parliament, a job currently held by Rao, Kesri said: "I need Manmohan Singh's help and apart from making him the member of CWC we might give him further responsibility".
